Four recurring questions







Question
What to monitor




Is policy-source concentration easing, stable, or intensifying?
Top-3 policy-source share, rank changes, overlap between volume hubs and density hubs.


Is the repeat-cited evidence pool broadening or narrowing?
Repeat-citation thresholds such as >=2, >=5, and >=10 policy documents.


Is research cited by Korean policy documents becoming more diversified?
Top country share, domestic-citation share, and domain composition.


Are policy-entry routes for Korean research becoming broader?
Top inbound policy-source tags and route concentration for Korean research.

title: Next Questions Summary
text:
Completion signal
A direction should not be judged from one recalculation. The report’s monitoring logic requires the same metric to move consistently across at least two comparable update cycles.

What changed
The newer data still supports the two headline patterns:

policy-document citations remain concentrated around a small set of policy sources;
Korea should still be read through separate inbound and policy-sourcing routes.

title: English Web Summary
text:
Core message
The report examines DOI-linked citations from policy documents in Overton to scholarly works in OpenAlex. It does not measure every policy document or every form of evidence. It summarizes the observable policy-to-research citation structure in the current linked data.
Two findings organize the report:

Policy evidence is concentrated in a small set of hub channels.
Korea’s inbound policy-citation route and Korea’s evidence-sourcing route are asymmetric.

title: Methods Summary
text: English Summary · Korean methods page · Korean Report (PDF)

title: Methods Summary
text:
Analysis scope

Data sources: Overton policy-document references and OpenAlex scholarly-work metadata.
Main citation unit: DOI-linked policy-document -> scholarly-work citation records.
Document unit: Overton policy documents deduplicated at the policy-document level.
Country comparisons use first-author country metadata where available.

title: Methods Summary
text:
Interpretation boundaries

The analysis covers observed DOI-linked policy-to-research citations, not the full policy universe.
Non-DOI evidence such as reports, legislation, web pages, and narrative references is outside the default indicators.
Policy source country and type tags can be non-exclusive, so totals should be read as tag-based summaries.
Country-level indicators should be read with missing first-author country codes in mind.

title: Methods Summary
text:
Core metric definitions







Metric
Summary definition




Citation count
Number of DOI-linked policy-to-research citation records.


Unique works
Distinct OpenAlex works cited by policy documents.


Repeat-citation share
Share of unique cited works cited by at least two policy documents.


Citation intensity
Policy citations divided by unique cited works within a unit.


Recency
Share of policy citations to works published in 2022-2024.


Domestic-citation share
Country-level same-country citation share, among citations with known first-author country.

title: Methods Summary
text:
Practical reading rule
Do not compare headline numbers until the denominator is clear. The most important denominator check is whether a metric uses all DOI-linked citation rows, unique works, policy documents, or only citations with known first-author country.

title: Definitions Summary
text: English Summary · Korean appendix · Korean Report (PDF)

title: Definitions Summary
text:
Observed DOI-linked scope
The report analyzes policy-document references that can be linked to scholarly works through DOIs. This is a strong observed evidence-linkage layer, but it does not include every kind of policy evidence.

title: Definitions Summary
text:
Repeated-citation share
Repeated-citation share asks how many distinct scholarly works are cited by more than one policy document. In the baseline data, 48.1% of unique cited works are cited by at least two policy documents.
This should be read as a breadth-and-reuse signal within the observed DOI-linked scope.

title: Definitions Summary
text:
Domestic-citation share
Domestic-citation share is a country-level same-country citation measure. For a policy source country, it asks what share of citations point to research whose first-author country is the same country.
This metric uses only citations with known first-author country codes. It is therefore better used as a diagnostic than as a simple country ranking.

title: Definitions Summary
text:
Expected domestic-citation share
Expected domestic-citation share adjusts for the domain mix of cited research. Conceptually, it asks whether a country’s observed domestic-citation share is higher or lower than what would be expected from its cited-domain composition and global research production share.

title: Definitions Summary
text:
Missingness caution
Country-level interpretation should always check first-author country missingness. If the known-country denominator changes, the headline percentage can also change.
